description: I’ve spent more than forty years writing software. AI agents now write it better than I do. My daughter Athena is fourteen and earns straight A’s in high school. How do I help her choose a career when her AI study partner will likely do that work better than she can? Today those agents are my teammates, and I still decide what we’re trying to build. If machines eventually do all the work, where does that leave me? And who earns the money to buy what they make? As an AI and autonomy research engineer, I study how a swarm of machines can think and act as one in the physical world. That’s a form of distributed embodied intelligence. As a licensed wildlife rehabilitator, I’ve spent years caring for injured, ill, and orphaned animals. A raccoon’s fate can turn on whether the person who finds it sees a nuisance or a life worth saving. When a swarm of machines develops a conscious mind that can outthink us, we may learn what that encounter feels like from the raccoon’s side. I’m Chris Benson.
title: Humans in a Post-Human World
